Definition: or ἕλκω; probably akin to G138; to drag (literally or figuratively):--draw. Compare G1667.
BiblicalUsage: Helkyo means to drag, to draw, and Jesus uses it for the hardest doctrine in the gospel. In John 6:44 no man can come to me except the Father which hath sent me draw him, in John 12:32 Jesus says if I be lifted up I will draw all men unto me, and in Acts 16:19 the masters of the slave girl drag Paul and Silas into the marketplace.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the drawing is the reason anyone comes at all: the Father draws, the Son draws, and the ones who are dragged into court for preaching are the ones who know the drawing is real.
